newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries steady in Tokyo, sentiment mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady in Tokyo, sentiment mixed.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little changed by midday Tokyo on Monday ahead of a Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday, traders said.
Light short-covering was spotted after Friday's falls in New York, with prices supported after the dollar bounced back against the yen to near New York closes after earlier losses.
But operators refrained from trading actively ahead of the FOMC meeting, they said.
Market sentiment was mixed as many operators were divided as to whether the Federal Reserve will raise its federal funds rate at the meeting, they said.
The key 30-year bond stood at 96-16/32, yielding 6.90 percent, compared with 95-15/32 in New York on Friday.
The June T-bond futures contract was up 2/32 at 110-1/32 compared with the previous close.
In New York, prices ended lower after the government reported a brisk pace of new housing starts in April.

"I think the Fed will not raise the FF rate this time. It seems that there is no immediate need to raise the rate looking at the results of the recent economic data," a dealer at a trust bank said. "The position of the market appears to be pretty much squared ahead of the FOMC meeting."
